findings.description: File header third line 'Redesigned from dark theme to Notion-canonical light aesthetic.' is narrative history, not a rule or actionable constraint. Describes the past state of the file rather than its current purpose. Remove or reduce to a single-line identifier.

Comment '/* Notion-canonical color tokens (exact values per task 20260517-071910) */' embeds a task tracking reference and the adjective 'canonical' adds no information beyond what the token names convey. Task IDs belong in commit messages, not stylesheet comments.

Comment '/* Card — Notion block style: background #ffffff, border 1px solid #e0e0e0, border-radius 4px, padding 8px */' duplicates the CSS values declared in the rule immediately below it. Redundant comments that restate already-visible code are verbosity violations. Delete the comment; the CSS is self-documenting.

Module header block (lines 1-11) contains a 5-item 'Responsibilities' narrative list. The imports at lines 13-18 already express the same information structurally. The preamble adds ~9 lines of story that must be maintained in sync with code. Trim to a 2-line identifier comment: module name + spec reference only.
findings.note: Pre-existing — not introduced in this diff. Tagged introduced_in_diff: false per Mechanism (ii).

findings.description: Inline comment '// Collect options from all meal slots, de-duped by option_id' restates what the immediately following for-loop and Set logic already shows. Same pattern at lines 205 ('// Empty state: all meal slots...') and 214 ('// Check selection: option is selected if ANY meal slot...'). These what-comments violate the 'comments explain why, not what' principle. Remove; the code is readable.

Comment '// Unified Meals group replaces separate breakfast/lunch/dinner groups' is a change-history note. It documents a past refactor, not a rule for the current code. Change history belongs in commit messages. Remove.

Two-line comment block '// Backend mutation handler key is "stage" with `to_stage` per save.py:69. / // Optimistic local update so renderApproveButton() disables immediately.' — the second line is a useful 'why' note and should stay. The first line cross-references an implementation detail of a sibling file that can drift out of sync; prefer removing line 537 and keeping line 539.

Module header block (lines 1-11) is 10 lines. Lines 6-10 contain a bulleted narrative describing the three runtime behaviors ('Tabs at top...', 'Tapping a candidate card...', 'Tapping a highlighted slot...'). Lines 9-11 add an explanatory note about matchMedia recomputation. The behavior description duplicates what the exported functions do; the matchMedia note is a useful 'why' but could be a 1-line inline at the call site. Trim header to 3 lines: module name, spec reference, breakpoint value.
findings.note: Pre-existing — not introduced in this diff.

findings.description: 3-line inline comment block (lines 147-149) inside _applyMobileLayout: 'ALWAYS collapse other panes on first mobile activation. The HTML scaffold ships with a tab pre-marked aria-pressed=true but no data-mobile-hidden on the panes, so without this call all three panes stack visibly.' This is legitimate 'why' context explaining a non-obvious invariant. It is NOT a verbosity violation — keep as-is.

Module header block (lines 1-7) is 6 lines. Lines 3-6 contain a 2-sentence explanation of slot-category matching behavior ('Card -> slot drop. Card carries data-option-id...'). This is borderline: it documents a non-trivial constraint that is not obvious from the function signatures. Minor at most — the constraint description could move to a 1-line comment inside _isCompatible instead of the file header.
findings.note: Pre-existing — not introduced in this diff.

findings.description: Module docstring (lines 1-11) contains 'Lock posture (codex Q2):' on line 8 — this is an internal design review annotation referencing a specific review question (codex Q2). Design rationale anchored to review sessions belongs in commit messages or design docs, not module docstrings. The posture itself ('per-trip lock held for the read-modify-write...') is useful context; only the 'codex Q2' attribution tag is noise. Remove the '(codex Q2)' attribution; keep the sentence.
findings.note: Pre-existing — not introduced in this diff.

findings.description: New function docstring for _get_existing_slot: 'Non-mutating slot lookup. Returns None if absent. Never calls setdefault.' This is a 1-line docstring that adds genuine value by contrasting with _get_or_create_slot's mutation behavior. The 'Never calls setdefault' clause is a valid rule, not a story. No violation — keep.

Inline comment '# Source option not found in origin slot: do not write invisible selected_option_id' (line 99) and identical comment at line 103 ('# Origin slot missing: do not write invisible selected_option_id') explain a non-obvious early-return guard. These are legitimate 'why' comments preventing a data integrity bug. Keep.
No verbosity violations found. HTML comments are minimal orientation labels (LEFT/CENTER/RIGHT panel, Populated by X). File is clean.

summary.overall_assessment: No critical or major verbosity violations. All 6 files are well below the 50-line minor threshold. The diff introduces 4 minor violations: (1) narrative 'redesigned from' note in main.css header, (2) task-ID annotation in main.css color token comment, (3) redundant value-restatement comment on .card rule in main.css, (4) what-comments and a change-history comment in state.js. Pre-existing minor violations exist in module headers of state.js, mobile.js, and drag.js and in the save.py module docstring, but these are not introduced by this diff. No file approaches the 50-line minor threshold — the largest concentration of verbose content is the state.js module header at ~9 lines. No action is blocking.
